title: SQL Server keyless CDC table: duplicate rows collapse, and an update removes the other copy

found.by: 2026-10-26 test round: SQL Server 2022 CU27, standard CDC through a gateway, one run

symptom: A table with two identical rows (1,a) lands one row at the snapshot. After one copy is updated to (1,c), the destination holds (1,c) and (2,b); the source holds (1,a), (1,c) and (2,b).
cause: For a keyless table the merge key is all its non-LOB columns, so identical rows count as one key.
effect: Duplicate rows are missing from the destination, and an update to one copy removes the other from it.
fix: Add a primary key before the first load (not tested here). Until then, compare the destination with the distinct source rows.
notes: One run. Which writer collapses the rows wasn't measured. The transaction replay in the same run matched the source.
